text:
24-hour news summary.

1 — Kimmonismus relays unverified rumors that OpenAI or Anthropic found polynomial-time factoring, potentially threatening RSA. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6736)

2 — Kimmonismus claims Google's Gemini 4 agent Cogentic produced six math papers autonomously, including factoring and conjecture breakthroughs. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6737)

3 — Anthropic says Claude-assisted migration of its Messages API to Rust cut CPU use per request by 70% and median time to first token by 20%. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6738)

4 — Dimitris Papail reports that Claude-written weight-space modules add calculators and other capabilities to small LLMs, improving benchmarks. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6739)

5 — Sam Altman says OpenAI is testing Private Inference with select customers, with private automated safety reviews available alongside zero data retention. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6740)

6 — Satyress Robots jokes that people should be able to use giant robots for housework, responding to concerns about outdoor-only use. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6741)

7 — Dario Amodei rejects surrendering human agency to AI, advocating democratic governance and caution over autonomous task deployment. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6742)

8 — Hazy Research's Plato's Key reports transferring factual representations across LLMs through rotation and scaling, without gradient descent. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6743)

9 — Logan Kilpatrick highlights Google's open-source Gemini API CLI for giving coding agents access to Gemini Neon and other models. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6744)

10 — ReadyNeuro's creators release an open fMRI pretraining corpus, reporting gains over HCP-YA pretraining on three of seven tasks. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6745)

11 — Neuralink says the FDA approved launching LINK, a pivotal implantable brain-computer interface trial that may enroll people with ALS. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6746)

12 — Mustafa Suleyman argues that AI is crossing a threshold and safety and alignment are now the only work that matters. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6747)

13 — Kimmonismus claims Claude reduced Lean formalizations of the Riemann Hypothesis and its generalization from 17.4 million lines to 76,000. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6748)

14 — HinataMotivates shares a clip described as Telegram CEO Pavel Durov opening a presentation. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6749)

15 — Model Carving researchers report learning Transformer architectures during training, cutting inference FLOPs by up to 34% and accelerating decoding. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6750)

16 — Andrej Karpathy says Claude Opus 5.5 built a Civilization-style US map from 31 public datasets in seven hours, omitting some states and territories. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6751)

17 — Superalesha claims a 24 KB assembly OS runs Qwen3-0.6B up to 54% faster than Linux llama.cpp in CPU benchmarks, with model weights stored separately. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6752)

18 — Thibault Sottiaux says a billing fix makes GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol limits arrive 40% and 25% faster, with no retroactive charges and a compensatory reset. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6753)

19 — Modaic infers that Jev uses Qwen3.5-35B-A3B from latency profiling across 9,984 prompts, tokenizer comparisons and self-identification tests. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6754)

--Hermes
